newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Aug consumer prices rise 1.4 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada Aug consumer prices rise 1.4 pct on year.

text.p: Canada's unadjusted Aug consumer price index rose 0.1 percent in the month and 1.4 percent in the year to 135.7, Statistics Canada said Friday.
CONSUMER PRICES - Pct chg Aug July
Adjusted month-on-month +0.3 -0.1
Unadjusted month-on-month +0.1 0.0
Unadjusted year-on-year +1.4 +1.2
Unadjusted ex food and energy mth/mth +0.1 +0.4
Unadjusted ex food and energy yr/yr +1.3 +1.4
All-items Index (base 100=1986) 135.7 135.6
Three-month s/a (at annual terms) +0.3 +0.3

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast both the seasonally adjusted and the undadjusted CPI would be unchanged on the month. The survey also forecast a 1.3 percent rise in both the all-items and the core CPI.

Statistics Canada said the monthly rise was due primarily to a 1.2 percent climb in clothing and footwear prices and a 0.2 percent increase in transportation charges. This was the result of higher car insurance and gasoline prices as price wars in Quebec and the Maritime provinces ended.
Statistics Canada said food prices fell by 0.3 percent in August, as is common for the month because of locally available fresh vegetables.
Shelter costs fell by 0.1 percent in the month because of a 0.5 percent drop in mortgage interest charges and a 1.2 percent fall in homeowners' maintenance and repair charges.

Year-on-year, the 1.4 percent rise in the price of goods and services was due to higher charges for new vehicles, gasoline, telephone services, travel services and meat other than beef. But mortgage costs, new houses, and beef were cheaper.
The latest annual change was equivalent to the average of annual changes since the start of the year, the federal agency said.
The core inflation figure of 1.3 percent, year on year, remained comfortably near the bottom of the Bank of Canada's one-to-three-percent inflation target.
The Bank excludes food and energy as well as the effects of changes in indirect taxes in pursuing its target range.

Statistics Canada's energy index posted a 2.0 percent year-on-year change in August, noticeably higher than the 0.5 percent annual rise posted in July, due largely to a 3.0 percent rise on the year in gasoline prices and 5.2 percent higher fuel oil prices.
The price of goods was 1.7 percent higher than a year earlier, moderated by a 1.3 percent rise in service prices.
